dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm glad you asked. I've decided to take your advice — I'm going to conduct an experiment!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: It's just a trial run, really... I'm going to try being a carefree, regular child for a day.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: A whole day!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess you have to start somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I even did a "warm-up" last night in preparation.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I closed all my books, put away my stationery, and kept reminding myself that there's no need to arrive at any conclusions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And then...?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Well, I was thinking about this as I lay in bed. What would a regular kid be doing right now? Listening to a story? Drawing? Drinking some warm milk before bed? Or maybe they'd already be asleep!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I stayed up so late thinking about it that this morning, I almost missed the optimal time to wake up naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're still overthinking things...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Mhm... I realized that, too. So, to remove all thought from the equation, I decided to make a "To-Do List for Kids."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what's on your list?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item one: toss and turn in bed (immediately after waking up). Then, get told to get up (do not get out of bed unprompted). Since there's no one to prompt me, I just pretend to be someone else and tell myself to get up.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: It isn't ideal, but I've decided it counts.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item two: be a fussy eater. I tried to find something to complain about, but I just couldn't bring myself to see it through.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: That's why I've written "item failed" on the list.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item three: snack uncontrollably. This one was the easiest, and my favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: ...But halfway through, I realized I'd made a mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: In the real world, no adult would ever actually let their child eat as much junk food as they wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item three: play meaningless games. This one was hard!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I ended up focusing all my attention on trying to find loopholes in the rules...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like things didn't go to plan...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Correct. So now I'm going to throw a tantrum!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm going to put away my to-do list and declare my experiment a huge failure! Then, I'm not going to make any effort whatsoever to learn from my mistakes!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I don't want to reflect on why I failed, and I don't want to listen to reason. I... just... don't... care!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is "throwing a tantrum" also on your list?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Eh!? How did you know?

choices.text: Because children are allowed to be unreasonable. It's in the job description.
So maybe your experiment was successful after all!
